primary.key: And when any one bringeth a meal-offering unto the LORD, his offering shall be of fine flour; and he shall pour oil upon it, and put frankincense thereon.
primary.s: After the burnt-offerings, the law turns to the offering of flour; Rashi, on 2:1, reads nefesh, soul, rendered ‘any one’, as the poor man who usually brings it, counted by God as though he offered his soul, and Ibn Ezra, on 2:1, as the soul named because this is a freewill gift and the soul is called willing.
primary.src: Rashi (Rosenbaum and Silbermann Hebrew, 1929 to 1934) and Ibn Ezra (Hebrew, On Your Way), on Leviticus 2:1, Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

basis.words: לֹא נֶאֱמַר נֶפֶשׁ בְּכָל קָרְבְּנוֹת נְדָבָה אֶלָּא בַּמִּנְחָה, מִי דַּרְכּוֹ לְהִתְנַדֵּב מִנְחָה? עָנִי. אָמַר הַקָּבָּ"ה, מַעֲלֶה אֲנִי עָלָיו כְּאִלּוּ הִקְרִיב נַפְשׁוֹ … נפש אדם והזכיר הנפש שהמנחה נדבה גם הנפש תקרא נדיבה ורוח נדיבה תסמכני
basis.gloss: [Rashi on 2:1, ‘and when a soul offers’:] Nefesh is not said of any freewill offering except the meal-offering. Who usually volunteers a meal-offering? The poor man. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I account it to him as though he offered his soul … [Ibn Ezra on 2:1, same words:] Nefesh means a person; and it names the soul because the meal-offering is a freewill offering, and the soul too is called willing: ‘and let a willing spirit uphold me’.

standby.key: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them: When any man of you bringeth an offering unto the LORD, ye shall bring your offering of the cattle, even of the herd or of the flock.
standby.s: The law of offerings, spoken from the tent of meeting, opens with herd and flock; Sforno, on 1:2, reads it as an offering from the offerer’s own self, in confession and humbling, since God has no desire for fools who sacrifice without first humbling themselves.
standby.src: Sforno, Commentary on the Torah, on Leviticus 1:2, Hebrew (On Your Way), Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

basis.words: אדם כי יקריב מכם. כי יקריב מעצמכם בוידוי דברים והכנעה על דרך ונשלמה פרים שפתינו וכאמרו זבחי אלהים רוח נשברה, כי אין חפץ בכסילים המקריבים בלתי הכנעה קודמת
basis.gloss: (Sforno on 1:2, ‘when any man of you bringeth’) When he offers of your own selves, by confession in words and humbling, in the manner of ‘so will we render for bullocks the offering of our lips’, and as it says, ‘the sacrifices of God are a broken spirit’; for there is no pleasure in fools who offer without humbling first.

primary.key: if the anointed priest shall sin so as to bring guilt on the people, then let him offer for his sin, which he hath sinned, a young bullock without blemish unto the LORD for a sin-offering.
primary.s: The law of the sin-offering for errors opens with the anointed priest; Rashi, on 4:3, reads his sin as the people’s guilt because they depend on him to atone and pray for them, and Sforno, on 4:3, as an error that befalls him only through the people’s own guilt, not from his heart.
primary.src: Rashi (Rosenbaum and Silbermann Hebrew, 1929 to 1934) and Sforno (Hebrew, On Your Way), on Leviticus 4:3, Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

basis.words: וּפְשׁוּטוֹ לְפִי אַגָּדָה: כְּשֶׁכֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל חוֹטֵא, אַשְׁמַת הָעָם הוּא זֶה, שֶׁהֵן תְּלוּיִין בּוֹ לְכַפֵּר עֲלֵיהֶם וּלְהִתְפַּלֵּל בַּעֲדָם, וְנַעֲשֶׂה מְקֻלְקָל … כלומר שלא תקרה לו שגגת חטאת זולתי ממוקשי עם, כאמרם (ברכות לד:) המתפלל וטעה סימן רע לו, ואם שליח ציבור הוא, סימן רע לשולחיו … כי לא מלבו היה החטא כלל, אבל קרה לו לאשמת העם
basis.gloss: [Rashi on 4:3, ‘if the anointed priest sin to the guilt of the people’, after the halakhic reading:] And its plain sense, following the aggadah: when the High Priest sins, this is the guilt of the people, for they depend on him to atone for them and to pray on their behalf, and he has become corrupted … [Sforno on 4:3, same words:] That is, an unwitting sin will not befall him except from the snares of the people, as the sages said: one who prays and errs, it is a bad sign for him, and if he is the emissary of the congregation, a bad sign for those who sent him … for the sin was not from his heart at all, but befell him for the guilt of the people.

standby.key: And if his means suffice not for a lamb, then he shall bring his forfeit for that wherein he hath sinned, two turtle-doves, or two young pigeons, unto the LORD: one for a sin-offering, and the other for a burnt-offering.
standby.s: For the oaths and uncleanness just listed, the law scales the offering to the sinner’s means; Ramban, on 5:7, explains the leniency, perhaps, by these oaths carrying no penalty of excision, and by the one defiled erring while doing a commandment, his mind on Heaven.
standby.src: Ramban, Commentary on the Torah, on Leviticus 5:7, Hebrew (On Your Way New), Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

basis.words: הקל הכתוב על החוטא באלו להביא קרבן עולה ויורד ויתכן שהטעם בשבועות מפני שאינן חייבי כריתות ובטומאת מקדש וקדשיו מפני שהוא טועה בדבר מצוה כי הכהן האוכל קדשים והבא למקדש להשתחוות או להקריב קרבן עוסק הוא במצוה ודעתו לשמים ולפיכך אע"פ שחטא בהעלמת הטומאה ריבה לו הכתוב כפרות
basis.gloss: (Ramban on 5:7, ‘and if his means suffice not for a lamb’) Scripture was lenient with the sinner in these cases, letting him bring an offering of higher or lower value. Perhaps the reason, for the oaths, is that they do not carry excision; and for the defilement of the Sanctuary and its holy things, that he errs in a matter of a commandment: the priest who eats holy food, or one who comes to the Sanctuary to bow or to bring an offering, is engaged in a commandment and his mind is on Heaven; therefore, although he sinned by forgetting his uncleanness, Scripture gave him more ways of atonement.

primary.key: If he offer it for a thanksgiving, then he shall offer with the sacrifice of thanksgiving unleavened cakes mingled with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil, and cakes mingled with oil, of fine flour soaked.
primary.s: Setting out the peace-offerings, the law turns to the offering of thanks; the Midrash, Leviticus Rabbah 9:7, reads it as lasting when all else ends: in the time to come every offering will cease but the thank-offering, and every prayer but thanksgiving.
primary.src: The Midrash, Leviticus Rabbah 9:7, the Torat Emet Hebrew text, Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

basis.words: רַבִּי פִּנְחָס וְרַבִּי לֵוִי וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּשֵׁם רַבִּי מְנַחֵם דְּגַלְיָא, לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא כָּל הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת בְּטֵלִין וְקָרְבַּן תּוֹדָה אֵינוֹ בָּטֵל, כָּל הַתְּפִלּוֹת בְּטֵלוֹת, הַהוֹדָאָה אֵינָהּ בְּטֵלָה
basis.gloss: (Leviticus Rabbah 9:7, placed on Leviticus 7:12) Rabbi Pinḥas, Rabbi Levi and Rabbi Yoḥanan in the name of Rabbi Menaḥem of Galya: in the time to come all the offerings will cease, but the thank-offering will not cease; all the prayers will cease, but thanksgiving will not cease.

standby.key: And he shall put off his garments, and put on other garments, and carry forth the ashes without the camp unto a clean place.
standby.s: The law of the burnt-offering turns to the altar’s ashes; Rashi, on 6:4, reads the change of clothes as no duty but decency, since clothes worn to cook for a master are not worn to pour his cup, and Ramban, on 6:4, as a commandment, a servant’s manners towards his master.
standby.src: Rashi (Rosenbaum and Silbermann Hebrew, 1929 to 1934) and Ramban (Hebrew, On Your Way New), on Leviticus 6:4, Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

basis.words: אֵין זוֹ חוֹבָה אֶלָּא דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, שֶׁלֹּא יְלַכְלֵךְ בְּהוֹצָאַת הַדֶּשֶׁן בְּגָדִים שֶׁהוּא מְשַׁמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן תָּמִיד … בְּגָדִים שֶׁבִּשֵּׁל בָּהֶן קְדֵרָה לְרַבּוֹ, אַל יִמְזֹג בָּהֶן כּוֹס לְרַבּוֹ … אבל לא ידעתי מנין אמר הרב שאינה חובה כי נראה שמצוה היא על הכהן שהבגדים שיעשה בהם הקרבנות גם הרמת הדשן יהיו בגדים נקיים לא ישמש באותן אשר הוציא הדשן והמצוה מדרך מוסר העבד לרבו
basis.gloss: [Rashi on 6:4, ‘and he shall put off his garments’:] This is not an obligation but a matter of decency, that he should not soil, in taking out the ashes, the garments in which he always ministers: garments in which one cooked a pot for his master, one should not pour his master a cup in them … [Ramban on 6:4, after quoting Rashi:] But I do not know where the Rabbi got that it is not an obligation, for it appears to be a commandment on the priest that the garments in which he performs the offerings, and the lifting of the ashes too, be clean garments, and that he not minister in those in which he took out the ashes; and the commandment is by way of a servant’s manners towards his master.

primary.key: Then Moses said unto Aaron: ‘This is it that the LORD spoke, saying: Through them that are nigh unto Me I will be sanctified, and before all the people I will be glorified.’ And Aaron held his peace.
primary.s: When fire from the LORD consumes Nadab and Abihu after their strange fire, Moses speaks to their father; Rashi, on 10:3, reads it as consolation, Moses having thought the sanctuary would be hallowed through himself or Aaron and now seeing the sons were greater, and Rashbam, on 10:3, as a charge not to mourn or leave the service.
primary.src: Rashi (Rosenbaum and Silbermann Hebrew, 1929 to 1934) and Rashbam (Hebrew, Daat edition), on Leviticus 10:3, Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

basis.words: אָמַר לוֹ מֹשֶׁה לְאַהֲרֹן, אַהֲרֹן אָחִי, יוֹדֵעַ הָיִיתִי שֶׁיִּתְקַדֵּשׁ הַבַּיִת בִּמְיֻדָּעָיו שֶׁל מָקוֹם, וְהָיִיתִי סָבוּר אוֹ בִי אוֹ בְךָ, עַכְשָׁיו רוֹאֶה אֲנִי שֶׁהֵם גְּדוֹלִים מִמֶּנִּי וּמִמְּךָ … אל תתאבל ואל תבכה ואל תחדל מן העבודה, כי הדבר הזה אשר אני אומר לך: הוא אשר דבר ה' בקרובי אקדש … וזה מוסר ואמיתת פשוטו. אבל האגדה שאומרת: שהיה מנחמו משה לאהרן … אין זה לפי הפשט
basis.gloss: [Rashi on 10:3, ‘this is it that the LORD spoke’:] Moses said to Aaron: Aaron my brother, I knew that the House would be hallowed through those intimate with the Omnipresent, and I thought it would be either through me or through you; now I see that they are greater than I and than you … [Rashbam on 10:3, ‘and Moses said unto Aaron’:] Do not mourn, do not weep, and do not cease from the service, for this thing that I tell you is what the LORD spoke: through them that are nigh unto Me I will be sanctified … [on ‘and Aaron held his peace’:] And this is the moral lesson and the truth of its plain sense. But the aggadah that says Moses was consoling Aaron … is not according to the plain sense.

standby.key: And Moses and Aaron went into the tent of meeting, and came out, and blessed the people; and the glory of the LORD appeared unto all the people.
standby.s: Aaron has brought the eighth day’s first offerings and given his blessing; Rashi, on 9:23, explains the entry, in one account, by Aaron’s distress, blaming himself, that the Divine Presence had not come down, until Moses went in and they prayed and it descended.
standby.src: Rashi, Commentary on the Torah, on Leviticus 9:23, Hebrew of the Rosenbaum and Silbermann edition (1929 to 1934), Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

basis.words: דָּ"אַ כֵּיוָן שֶׁרָאָה אַהֲרֹן שֶׁקָּרְבוּ כָּל הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת וְנַעֲשׂוּ כָל הַמַּעֲשִׂים וְלֹא יָרְדָה שְׁכִינָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, הָיָה מִצְטַעֵר וְאוֹמֵר, יוֹדֵעַ אֲנִי שֶׁכָּעַס הַקָּבָּ"ה עָלַי וּבִשְׁבִילִי לֹא יָרְדָה שְׁכִינָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, אָמַר לוֹ לְמֹשֶׁה, מֹשֶׁה אָחִי, כָּךְ עָשִֹיתָ לִי שֶׁנִּכְנַסְתִּי וְנִתְבַּיַּשְׁתִּי? מִיַּד נִכְנַס מֹשֶׁה עִמּוֹ וּבִקְּשׁוּ רַחֲמִים וְיָרְדָה שְׁכִינָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
basis.gloss: (Rashi on 9:23, ‘and Moses and Aaron went in’, after a first explanation, that Moses went in to teach Aaron the incense) Another explanation: when Aaron saw that all the offerings had been brought and all the rites performed, and the Divine Presence had not come down to Israel, he was distressed and said: I know that the Holy One, blessed be He, is angry with me, and on my account the Divine Presence has not come down to Israel. He said to Moses: Moses my brother, is this what you have done to me, that I entered and have been put to shame? At once Moses went in with him, and they asked for mercy, and the Divine Presence came down to Israel.

primary.key: All the days wherein the plague is in him he shall be unclean; he is unclean; he shall dwell alone; without the camp shall his dwelling be.
primary.s: The law of the skin plague turns to the one declared unclean; Rashi, on 13:46, with the rabbis, explains why he alone of the unclean dwells apart: having parted husband from wife and friend from friend by slander, he too is parted.
primary.src: Rashi, Commentary on the Torah, on Leviticus 13:46, Hebrew of the Rosenbaum and Silbermann edition (1929 to 1934), Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

basis.words: בדד ישב. שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ טְמֵאִים יוֹשְׁבִין עִמּוֹ; וְאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ מַה נִּשְׁתַּנָּה מִשְּׁאָר טְמֵאִים לֵישֵׁב בָּדָד? הוֹאִיל וְהוּא הִבְדִּיל בְּלָשׁוֹן הָרָע בֵּין אִישׁ לְאִשְׁתּוֹ וּבֵין אִישׁ לְרֵעֵהוּ, אַף הוּא יִבָּדֵל
basis.gloss: (Rashi on 13:46, ‘he shall dwell alone’) That other unclean persons shall not dwell with him. And our rabbis said: how does he differ from other unclean persons, that he must dwell alone? Since he, by evil speech, made a separation between a man and his wife and between a man and his fellow, he too shall be separated.

standby.key: And the leper in whom the plague is, his clothes shall be rent, and the hair of his head shall go loose, and he shall cover his upper lip, and shall cry: ‘Unclean, unclean.’
standby.s: Closing the priest’s inspections of the skin plague, the law turns to the one pronounced unclean; Ibn Ezra, on 13:45, reads the rent clothes either as a mark to know him by or as mourning for his evil deeds, for which the plague came.
standby.src: Ibn Ezra, Commentary on the Torah, on Leviticus 13:45, Hebrew (On Your Way), Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

basis.words: בגדיו יהיו פרומים. כמו קרועים להכירו ללכת במנהג משונה או טעמו כענין אבל על כן בגדיו יהיו פרומים וראשו פרוע והטעם שיתאבל על רוע מעשיו כי בעבור מעשיו בא לו זה הנגע
basis.gloss: (Ibn Ezra on 13:45, ‘his clothes shall be rent’) Perumim is like ‘torn’: so that he be recognised, going about in an unusual manner; or its sense is like that of a mourner, and therefore his clothes shall be rent and his head loose, and the reason is that he mourn for the evil of his deeds, for because of his deeds this plague came upon him.
